answer: Each new agent enters as a vertex that must lock a slashable bond and pay for a verifiable compute proof before it can transact. Creating one identity is cheap, but a thousand fake vertices each need their own bond and proof, so attack cost grows linearly while honest cost stays flat. If linked fakes misbehave, the penalty sends a ripple through their shared funding source and burns the bonds, like a willow losing every branch fed by one poisoned root.
